description: This dataset gives the locations of combined sewer overflow outfalls in New York State, published by the state environmental conservation department as an ArcGIS feature layer and on the data.ny.gov CSO map. Combined sewers collect stormwater runoff, domestic sewage and industrial wastewater in one pipe to a treatment facility and are designed to overflow to a water body in heavy rain. The item says there are about 800 CSO outfalls in the state, down from about 1,300 in 1993 because of abatements by permittees, and advises the public to avoid contact with water near a CSO during or after rain or snowmelt. The item links a metadata download that describes how the data were created and the attributes. Coverage: statewide outfall locations; the item was modified in 2026. Access: free; DEC asks for credit in derived products, does not allow secondary distribution, and requires the documentation to be used with the data. Caveats: locations only in the description, with no overflow volumes, and the redistribution restriction limits reuse. It supports overflow exposure and abatement scenarios for combined sewer systems, and relates to the Canadian CSO volumes and EPA sewer overflow event records in the catalogue.
